claims.text: Increasing atomic size mismatch through controlled compositional substitution enhances local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions caused by atomic size mismatch impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength.
Increasing atomic size mismatch reduces ductility relative to an alloy with minimal mismatch.
The proposed initial material is a homogenized, single-phase multi-component concentrated alloy with secondary-phase and texture effects minimized.
Composition can be varied systematically to increase atomic size mismatch while retaining a similar phase and chemical distribution.
The proposed comparison is conducted at room temperature under quasi-static uniaxial tensile or compression loading.
Atomic size mismatch induces local lattice distortions.
Enhanced lattice distortions create local stress fields.
The local stress fields associated with lattice distortions impede dislocation motion.
Alloys with greater atomic size mismatch will have higher yield strength than the baseline alloy.
Alloys with greater atomic size mismatch will have lower ductility than the baseline alloy.
The baseline is a multi-component concentrated alloy having minimal atomic size mismatch.
The proposed relationship is limited to single-phase multi-component alloys tested at ambient temperature and moderate deformation rates.
Phase separation or extreme temperature or strain-rate conditions may produce different behavior.
The quantitative effect of atomic size mismatch on mechanical properties may vary among alloy systems.
Strength and ductility may also be influenced by strengthening mechanisms other than lattice distortion.
A controlled series should incrementally increase atomic size mismatch while holding other microstructural features consistent.
Local lattice strain fields and dislocation structures can be assessed using diffraction or local-probe methods and electron microscopy.
The hypothesis is falsified if increasing mismatch does not consistently raise yield strength and lower ductility, or if enhanced lattice distortion and dislocation pinning are not observed.
